chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus'adat ibn Sadaqah, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father (peace be upon them both) who said:

God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said, "Four acts will make the heart perish: committing sins continuously; talking with women often; arguing with a fool, (since you keep talking with him, but he will never be guided to the right way), and associating with the dead!" They asked him what he meant by the dead? The Prophet of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, "All the rich who live in ease and luxury."

key_terms.الذَّنْبُ عَلَى الذَّنْبِ: Committing sins continuously or one after another
key_terms.الْمَوْتَى: The dead (metaphorically referring to the rich and luxurious)
key_terms.مُمَارَاةَ الْأَحْمَقِ: Arguing or disputing with a fool
key_terms.مُنَاقَشَةِ النِّسَاءِ: Frequent conversation or discussion with women

ai.seo_question: What are the four acts that kill the heart according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these four spiritual killers in *Al-Khisal*, emphasizing how internal decay stems from both moral negligence and social missteps. Notably, the Hadith offers a unique Shia interpretation of 'the dead' not as the physically deceased, but as the spiritually lifeless wealthy who are engrossed in worldly luxury, a concept resonating with the critique of *al-muftrun* in the Quran.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-65 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Harun ibn Muslim, on the authority of Mus’adat ibn Sadaqah, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB) that

God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Four acts will make the heart perish: committing sins continuously; talking with women often; arguing with a fool, (since you keep talking with him, but he will never be guided to the right way), and associating with the dead!” They asked him what he meant by the dead? The Prophet of God (MGB) said, “All the rich who live in ease and luxury.”
